'''Nina Byers''' (January 19, 1930 – June 5, 2014) was a theoretical physicist, research professor and professor of physics emeritus in the department of physics and astronomy, UCLA,<ref name=Byers_home>{{cite web|title=Nina Byers|url=http://www.pa.ucla.edu/directory/nina-byers|work=UCLA Physics & Astronomy directory|publisher=University of California Los Angeles|access-date=29 March 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111192445/http://www.pa.ucla.edu/directory/nina-byers|archive-date=11 November 2013}}</ref> and Fellow of [[Somerville College, Oxford]]. She is known for proving the [[Byers–Yang theorem]], together with [[Yang Chen-Ning|C.N. Yang]].

==Contributions==
Byers received a B.A. from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1950 and a Ph.D. from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1956.<ref name=UCLAobit>{{cite web|last1=Rozenzweig|first1=James|title=Nina Byers|url=http://www.pa.ucla.edu/content/nina-byers|website=UCLA Physics & Astronomy|publisher=University of California Los Angeles|access-date=27 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425202302/http://www.pa.ucla.edu/content/nina-byers|archive-date=25 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=Byers_contributions>{{cite web|first=Nina|last=Byers|title=Byers, Nina|url=http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Byers,_Nina@931234567.html|work=CWP|publisher=University of California Los Angeles|access-date=29 March 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016133230/http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Byers,_Nina@931234567.html|archive-date=16 October 2014}}</ref>

Byers made phenomenological analyses of experimental observations leading to theoretical advances in [[particle physics]] and the theory of [[superconductivity]]. In "Theoretical considerations concerning quantized magnetic flux in superconductors," she showed that observation of [[flux quantization]] in superconductors in units of hc/2e is experimental evidence for the [[Cooper pairing]] of electrons proposed by the [[BCS theory]] of superconductivity ([[Byers-Yang theorem]]).<ref name=Byers_contributions/>

In addition to scientific papers, Byers published papers and edited a book on original and important contributions to modern physics by 20th century female physicists. She developed the website ''Contributions of 20th Century Women to Physics'' (CWP website), which documents original and important contributions to physics by over 80 female physicists of the 20th century.<ref>{{cite web|title=Contributions of 20th century women to physics|url=http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/|publisher=University of California Los Angeles|access-date=29 March 2014}}</ref> With Gary Williams,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pa.ucla.edu/directory/gary-williams |title=Gary Williams, UCLA Physics & Astronomy |access-date=2014-09-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519130947/http://www.pa.ucla.edu/directory/gary-williams |archive-date=2018-05-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> she edited a book based on data from the website that expands the biographies and describes more fully the scientific contributions of forty distinguished 20th century female physicists.<ref>{{cite book|editor-last=Byers|editor-first=Nina|title=Out of the shadows : contributions of twentieth-century women to physics|date=2010|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge|isbn=9780521169622|editor2-last=Williams |editor2-first=Gary}}</ref>

Byers was elected to many offices in The [[American Physical Society]] (APS) and [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS), including President of the APS Forum on History of Physics (2004–2005), APS Forum on Physics and Society (1982), and APS Councilor-at-large of the Society (1977–81).<ref name=Byers_contributions/>
